contexts:
[1] Siemens Manual Vertical Induction Motors EN, p. 23 · Thrust Bearing
Principle elements of the Kingsbury-type thrust bearing are the rotating thrust runner and the stationary pivotal thrust shoes (See Figure 7) The runner is the highly polished bottom surface of the thrust block and receives the thrust load through a massive nut above the thrust block threaded on the top end of the shaft. The pivotal thrust shoes are faced with tin-hard Babbitt and machined to form an accurate surface plate.
During operation, the thrust bearing revolves in an oil bath which covers the bearing. Each shoe is free to tilt slightly in any direction and sets itself by pivoting at a minute angle causing a wedge-shaped film of oil to form between the shoe and the runner. An end play of 0.012 - 0.017 inches is preset at the factory by shims between the thrust plate and the upper guide (upthrust) bearing.

[2] Nidec Motor Manual, p. 24 · I. Spherical Roller Thrust Bearings and Angular Contact Bearings (With Springs)
On spherical roller or angular contact thrust bearings with springs, setting the correct end play for preload requires a controlled assembly method, due to various deflections internal to the motor and friction of locknut threads from spring force. An end play setting of .005 to .008 inches is required to allow the lower guide bearing to return to an unload position when external thrust is applied to the motor (see Figure 5). End play can be properly adjusted by the following recommended procedure:
- A. Place spring retainer, without springs and lower thrust washer of bearing, into upper bracket bearing bore.
- B. Using a depth micrometer, measure the distance between the top of the lower thrust washer and the faced surface on top of the bearing housing. Record this dimension to three decimal places.
- C. Add .005 and .008 inches to the recorded dimension to obtain the correct minimum and maximum settings range for the unit.
- D. Reassemble bearing with springs; motor is now ready to set end play.
NOTE: Certain motor builds require removal of the fabricated steel or cast aluminum oil baffle to provide access for depth micrometer measurements.
Motors built with spherical roller thrust or angular contact bearings with springs require a minimum external thrust load, sufficient to compress upper die springs and unload lower guide bearing from axial spring thrust. Refer to the motor's spring thrust plate for required minimum thrust.
NOTE: Do not run motor without load for more than fifteen minutes, as lower bearing damage may occur and improper seating of thrust bearing may cause vibration.

[3] Nidec Motor Manual, p. 24 · 2. Angular Contact Ball Bearings (Without Springs)
- A. No preliminary measurements are required to set end play. End play may be set by any of the following methods described in this section.
- B. To correctly adjust the rotor end play setting on units with angular contact ball bearings, a dial indicator should be positioned to read the shaft axial movement. (See figure 7 for location of dial indicator.) The rotor adjusting locknut should be turned until no further upward movement of the shaft is indicated. The locknut is then loosened until .005 to .008 end play is obtained, lock the locknut with the lockwasher.
- C. Motors that have two opposed angular contact bearings, locked on the mount for up and down thrust, do not require rotor end play adjustment. The shaft, however, must be set to original "AH" (shaft extension) to prevent the guide bearing in the lower bracket from taking external thrust.

Figures for this passage:
- FIGURE7 (METHOD1&3) — image path: diagrams/ecc5861a-047f-4623-bbf0-679bffbfde8f/fig7_1.png

[4] Siemens Manual Vertical Induction Motors EN, p. 22 · End Play
Machines designed for applications involving primarily continuous heavy downthrust but having momentary upthrust are equipped with angular contact or spherical roller bearings. Spherical roller bearings may be preloaded with springs (See Figure 8). The end play is most often 0.005 to 0.008 in. but see the motor outline for the exact value for your motor. The bottom bearing takes the momentary upthrust and prevents reverse loading of the top bearings. End play is limited by shims when the thrust block is shrunk on the shaft or by tightening the locknut on the shaft above the bearing mounting sleeve. The thrust bearings on 2 pole motors are mounted directly on the shaft and do not require an adjustment by the shims or locknut.

[5] Siemens Manual Vertical Induction Motors EN, p. 23 · Lower Guide Bearing
The function of the lower guide bearing with a Kingsbury-type bearing is to provide radial location of the shaft with no thrust or end play limit. This bearing may be one of three types - grease-lubricated ball bearing, oil-lubricated ball bearing, or oil-lubricated sleeve bearing (See Figures 9, 10 and 11).

results.question: For a hollow shaft Siemens motor, what dial indicator reading is the limit for acceptable alignment?
results.expected_answer: Readings must not exceed 0.0005 inches at 90-degree increments
results.rewritten_query: What is the maximum dial indicator reading for acceptable alignment of a hollow shaft Siemens motor?
results.answer:
The limit for acceptable dial indicator reading for alignment of a hollow shaft Siemens motor is 0.0005 inches. 

### Procedure for Alignment
1. Clamp dial indicator to the pump shaft, aligning it with the basebolt plane, and set the dial indicator to zero.
2. Remove the top cover and rotate both the unit and pump shafts.
3. Read the dial indicator at 90-degree increments from the starting point.
4. Ensure the indicator readings do not exceed 0.0005 inches for acceptable alignment.
5. Shim flange faces if necessary.
6. Once alignment and vibration are within limits, engage the drive and run the unit at minimum load, checking for vibration. Continue increasing load and checking vibration until full load is obtained.

### Key Considerations
- Accurate alignment is critical as the pump shaft acts as a pendulum supported by the coupling and bearing.
- Misalignment can lead to excessive vibration and potential damage to the motor components.

For the relevant values, refer to [2].

results.rewritten_query: What is the recommended drying temperature for Siemens Class F insulation, and what preparatory steps are required before reaching this temperature?
results.answer:
The drying temperature specified by Siemens for Class F insulation is 245°F (118°C) [1]. 

Before reaching this temperature, the following procedures must be performed:

1. Bake at 70% of the specified temperature to avoid steam inside the winding for about six hours.
2. After this initial period, the temperature can be raised to the drying temperature of 245°F (118°C) [1]. 

This gradual approach helps to ensure a thorough drying process without damaging the insulation.

results.answer:
When shimming between flanges on a Siemens vertical motor, minor shims should be one-half the thickness of the major shim. Shims should not penetrate deeper than the bolt hole circle and not be wider than twice the penetration distance [1].

- **Minor Shim Thickness**: One-half the thickness of the major shim.
- **Shim Penetration**: 
  - Maximum penetration depth: No deeper than the bolt hole circle.
  - Maximum width: No wider than twice the penetration distance.

[1] ABB Manual for Induction Motors and Generators EN, p. 85 · 7.5.3.3 Re-greasing intervals
Rolling bearings of electrical machines need to be re-greased at regular intervals. The re-greasing interval is found on the bearing plate.
NOTE:
Regardless of the re-greasing interval, the bearings need to be re-greased at least once per year.
The re-greasing intervals are calculated for an operating temperature of 70°C (160°F). If the operating temperature is lower or higher than the assumed, the re-grease interval has to be altered accordingly. Higher operating temperature decreases the re-greasing interval.
NOTE:
An increase in the ambient temperature raises the temperature of the bearings correspondingly. The values for the re-greasing interval should be halved for every 15°C (30°F) increase in bearing temperature and may be once doubled for a 15°C (30°F) decrease in bearing temperature.

[2] ABB Manual for Induction Motors and Generators EN, p. 84 · 7.5.2.5 Oil change schedule for mineral oils
For self-lubricated bearings cleaning intervals with oil changes of approximately 8000 operating hours are recommended and approx. 20000 operating hours for bearings with oil circulation systems.
Shorter oil change intervals may be necessary in case of frequent start-ups, high oil temperatures or excessively high contamination due to external influences.
The correct oil change interval can be found on the bearing plate and dimensional drawing, see Chapter 2.1.2 Bearing plate.

NOTE:
Start-up greasing may take several grease portions (3-10 times amount mentioned at the lubrication plate).
The re-lubrication interval will never be longer than 12 months.
The type of original grease used is found on the bearing plate on the machine. Acceptable types of grease can be found in Chapter 7.5.3 Rolling bearings.
NOTE:
Do not mix greases! There must be only one type of grease inside the bearing - not mixture of two or more greases.
The temperature of the bearings will initially increase because of the excess grease. After few hours, the excess grease will be discharged through the lubrication valve and the temperature of the bearing will return to normal running temperature.
If available, and after the machine has been running for several hours, measure the vibrations or SPM-values from the SPM-nipples, and record the values for future reference use.

results.question: What is the tightening torque for an M20 strength class 8.8 standard-thread screw on the Kohler KD27V12 engine?
results.rewritten_query: What is the tightening torque specification for an M20 strength class 8.8 standard-thread screw on the Kohler KD27V12 engine?
results.answer:
The tightening torque for an M20 strength class 8.8 standard-thread screw on the Kohler KD27V12 engine is 390 Nm. 

### Reasoning
This value comes from the tightening torques table for metric standard thread, which specifies the following for an M20 screw of strength class 8.8:

| Standard thread - Strength class | Tightening torque - 8.8 |
| - | - |
| M20 | 390 Nm |

Verification of tightening torques is important to prevent sudden and severe damage to machinery, as indicated in the ABB manual recommendation to regularly verify the tightness of fastenings, particularly for critical components like anchor bolts [2]. 

### Procedure
1. Verify that you have the correct size and strength class of screw.
2. Clean the threads of both the screw and the corresponding hole.
3. Apply anti-seize or oil if specified for the application (noted as "oiled" in general guidelines).
4. Use a calibrated torque wrench set to 390 Nm.
5. Slowly tighten the screw while monitoring the torque reading.
6. Ensure that the screw is tightened to the specified torque without exceeding it.

Note that the tightening torque values are crucial to ensure the integrity and safety of the engine's components.

[5] Nidec Motor Manual, p. 33 · Winding Thermostats
Winding thermostats are snap action, bi-metallic, temperature actuated switches. Their purpose is to activate a warning device, or simply shut down the motor upon excessive winding temperatures, when wired into the motor control circuit.
Thermostats are made either with contacts that are normally closed (open at high temperatures) or contacts that are normally open (closed at high temperatures). The thermostat temperature switch point is pre-calibrated by the manufacturer and is not adjustable. Reset is automatic after a decrease in temperature. Thermostats are normally installed in the connection end turns of the motor winding. Standard procedure is to wire three thermostats together in a set, with one thermostat embedded in each phase of the winding. Open thermostats are normally wired in parallel, while closed thermostats are wired in series. Refer to the figure below for further explanation.

results.question: If the fuel sulfur content is between 0.5% and 1%, how does the Kohler engine oil change interval change?
results.expected_answer: Oil change factor 1/2 — the interval is halved; limited to engine oil categories 2 and 3
results.rewritten_query: How does a fuel sulfur content of 0.5% to 1% affect the oil change interval for Kohler engines?
results.answer:
If the fuel sulfur content is between 0.5% and 1%, the Kohler engine oil change interval will be reduced by half. This adjustment is indicated by the oil change factor of "1/2" for that specific sulfur content range.

### Summary of Changes
- **Sulfur Content Range:** \(0.5 < \text{Sulfur content} \leq 1\% \)
- **Oil Change Factor:** "1/2" (reduces the maintenance interval by half) [1][3].

### Reasoning
The reduction in the oil change interval is necessary to account for the increased stress on the engine oil due to the higher sulfur content in the fuel, which can affect oil performance.

### Procedure for Adjustment
1. Determine the basic oil change interval from the maintenance tables based on the genset application (ESP, PRP, COP) and engine injection calibration (EO or FO).
2. Apply the oil change factor of "1/2" to the determined basic change interval:
   - New Change Interval = Basic Change Interval × (1/2).

Note: If there are difficulty factors or more challenging operating conditions, validate the oil change interval through an engine oil analysis [1].

[5] Nidec Motor Manual, p. 22 · Delta Connected Motor:
Using an ohmmeter, identify the three groups of three leads. Separate these groups by tying them with tape. Attach leads to a pair of wires in a group, and observe the voltage drop from each pair of energized leads to the third lead in that group. Continue until a combination is found that gives a voltage drop from each of the energized leads to the third lead equal to one half of the battery voltage. The lead located halfway between the other two will thus be the corner lead of the delta. Repeat this for each group of leads, marking the corner leads #1, #2, and #3.
Next, use the inductive kick test method to identify the proper markings for the other two leads of each group. The two coils #3 & #6 and 3 & #8, acting in parallel, will produce the effect of a coil positioned halfway between the actual position of the two coils. The flux produced by #3 & #6 and #3 & #8 combined, will be perpendicular to the axis of #1 & #4 and #2 & #7. Opening and closing a switch in this circuit will produce a kick in coils #1 & #9 and #2 & #5, but no kick in #1 & #4 and #2 & #7.
Therefore, if the battery is connected from #3 & #6 and #3 & #8 as shown, opening and closing the battery circuit, the voltmeter will identify leads #1, #4, and #9 and can be distinguished by noting the magnitude rather than the polarity. The voltmeter can then be connected to terminal #2 for determination of the leads #5 & #7. Leads #2 to #7 will give little or no deflection, and leads #2 to #5 will give a substantial
deflection.
In succession, the battery is then transferred to the corner of #1. Tie the battery between leads #1 & #4 & #9. Making and breaking the circuit will be perpendicular to #3 & #8 and #2 & #5, resulting in no deflection. However, there will be a deflection from leads #2 & #7 and #3 & #6. Placing the battery next on the #2 & #5 and #2 & #7 leads will be perpendicular to #1 & #9 and #3 & #6 leads, therefore creating no deflection. Leads #1 & #4 and #3 & #8 would then have a deflection, thus concluding the lead testing of
the nine lead delta connected motor.

results.question: What is the correct charge generator belt tension on the EMSA generator, and when must it be reset?
results.expected_answer: 535 N (120 lb); if the tension is below 250 N (56 lb), reset it to 535 N
results.rewritten_query: What is the correct belt tension for the EMSA generator's charge generator, and when should it be reset?
results.answer:
The correct charge generator belt tension on the EMSA generator must be tightened to 22 Nm (16 lb ft) after adjusting the alternator position. This adjustment is necessary to either increase or decrease belt tension as required, which can be done by loosening the pivot bolt and the connecting bolt of the charge generator, moving the alternator, and then re-tightening the bolts to the specified torque value. The specific procedure is as follows:

1. Loosen the pivot bolt of the charge generator.
2. Loosen the connecting bolt.
3. Move the alternator to adjust the belt tension.
4. Tighten the charge generator pivot bolt and connecting bolt to 22 Nm (16 lb ft) [2]. 

It's important to regularly check and reset the belt tension to ensure proper operation, especially if performance issues arise or if the V-ribbed belt seems loose.

results.question: What torque does EMSA specify for the charge generator pivot bolt and connecting bolt after adjusting the belt?
results.rewritten_query: What is the specified torque for the charge generator pivot bolt and connecting bolt according to EMSA after adjusting the belt?
results.answer:
The torque specified by EMSA for the charge generator pivot bolt and connecting bolt after adjusting the belt is 22 Nm (16 lb ft) [1]. 

### Procedure for Adjusting Belt Tension:
1. Loosen the pivot bolt of the charge generator.
2. Loosen the connecting bolt.
3. Move the alternator to increase or decrease the belt tension.
4. Tighten the charge generator pivot bolt and connecting bolt to 22 Nm (16 lb ft).

This procedure ensures that the belt tension is properly adjusted and that both bolts are securely fastened to the specified torque value.

results.question: What fuel pipe diameter does EMSA recommend for an 800–1500 kVA standby generator, and what are the pipe length and height limits?
results.expected_answer: 1 1/2 inch; maximum 6 m length, 0.9 m vertical height, 6 pipe fittings
results.rewritten_query: What is the recommended fuel pipe diameter for an EMSA 800–1500 kVA standby generator, and what are the maximum pipe length and height limits?
results.answer:
For an 800–1500 kVA standby generator, EMSA recommends the following fuel pipe specifications:

| Parameter                            | Value     |
|--------------------------------------|-----------|
| Recommended Pipe Diameter             | 1 1/2"    |
| Maximum Length of the Fuel Pipe      | 6 m       |
| Maximum Vertical Height              | 0.9 m     |
| Maximum Number of Pipe Fittings      | 6         |

### Reasoning and Procedure
1. Ensure that the fuel pipe diameter is 1 1/2 inches as recommended.
2. Confirm that the length of the fuel pipe does not exceed 6 meters.
3. Verify that the vertical height does not exceed 0.9 meters.
4. Limit the number of pipe fittings to a maximum of 6.

These specifications help ensure proper fuel flow and pressure for the generator's operation while minimizing potential issues with fuel supply. Proper installation according to these limits is crucial for optimal generator performance [1].

results.question: When adding electrolyte to an EMSA maintenance-type battery for the first time, what density and level are required, and how long is the minimum charge?
results.expected_answer: Specific density 1.280 at 20°C, filled to 15 mm above the plates (electrolyte above 10°C); minimum charging period 6 hours
results.rewritten_query: What is the required electrolyte density and level for EMSA maintenance-type batteries during the initial fill, and what is the minimum charging duration?
results.answer:
To add electrolyte to an EMSA maintenance-type battery for the first time, the following guidelines need to be followed:

1. **Electrolyte Level**: The electrolyte should be added so that it is 10 mm above the plates. 
2. **Density Measurement**: There are specific density ranges for the state of charge when measuring with a hydrometer:
   - Fully charged: 1.270 - 1.280
   - Half charged: 1.220 - 1.230
   - Discharged: 1.150 - 1.220 [2][3].
3. **Charging Duration**: The battery should be monitored for a change in electrolyte level every 1 hour; if no change is observed, the charging process is considered complete after 1 hour. [1].

**Procedure to Add Electrolyte**:
1. Ensure that the battery plates are checked and ready.
2. Prepare distilled water to add along with the electrolyte.
3. Fill the electrolyte to a level 10 mm above the plates.
4. Begin charging the battery.
5. Monitor the electrolyte level every hour.
6. If there's no change in electrolyte level after 1 hour, the battery is considered fully charged [1].

This process ensures the battery is adequately filled and charged for optimal performance.

The connections of the main power cables must be designed to withstand demanding operation conditions where the insulators can be subjected to dirt, humidity and surge voltages. In order to ensure lasting and trouble-free running, it is therefore important that the length of the insulation and creepage distances are sufficient. The minimum insulation and creepage distances should be equal or exceed demands set by:

- Standards
- Classification rules
- Hazardous area classification.
The insulation and creepage distances apply both for insulation distances between two different phases, and for insulation distances between one phase and earth. The air insulation distance is the shortest distance through air between two points with different electrical potential (voltage). [1] ABB Manual for Induction Motors and Generators EN, p. 86 · Automatic re-greasing
A variety of automatic re-lubrication systems is available on the market. However, ABB recommends only the use of electromechanical re-lubrication systems. The quality of the grease entering the bearing has to be checked at least once per year: the grease has to look and feel like new grease. Any separation of the base oil from the soap is not acceptable.
NOTE:
If an automatic re-greasing system is used, double the amount of grease indicated on the bearing plate.

[2] ABB Manual for Induction Motors and Generators EN, p. 22 · Following figure for bearing type: Rolling bearing

NOTE:
NOTE:
Start-up greasing may take several grease portions (3-10 times amount mentioned at the lubrication plate).
The re-lubrication interval will never be longer than 12 months.
The type of original grease used is found on the bearing plate on the machine. Acceptable types of grease can be found in Chapter 7.5.3 Rolling bearings.
NOTE:
Do not mix greases! There must be only one type of grease inside the bearing - not mixture of two or more greases.
The temperature of the bearings will initially increase because of the excess grease. After few hours, the excess grease will be discharged through the lubrication valve and the temperature of the bearing will return to normal running temperature.
If available, and after the machine has been running for several hours, measure the vibrations or SPM-values from the SPM-nipples, and record the values for future reference use.

For self-lubricated bearings cleaning intervals with oil changes of approximately 8000 operating hours are recommended and approx. 20000 operating hours for bearings with oil circulation systems.
Shorter oil change intervals may be necessary in case of frequent start-ups, high oil temperatures or excessively high contamination due to external influences.
The correct oil change interval can be found on the bearing plate and dimensional drawing, see Chapter 2.1.2 Bearing plate.

The machines are equipped with sleeve bearings with a very long service life provided that the lubrication functions continuously and that the oil type and quality are as per ABB recommendations, and that the oil change instructions are followed.

[1] ABB Manual for Induction Motors and Generators EN, p. 86 · 7.5.3.5 Bearing grease (table)
It is essential to use grease of good quality and with the correct base soap. This will ensure a long and trouble free lifetime of the bearings.
Grease used for re-greasing should have the following properties:
- Be special rolling bearing grease.
- Be of good quality with a lithium complex soap, and with mineral-, or PAO-oil.
- Have a base oil viscosity of 100 to 160 cSt at 40°C (105°F).
- Have a consistency NLGI grade between 1.5 and 3. For vertically or in hot conditions mounted machines, NLGI grade 2 or 3 is recommended.
- Have a continuous temperature range between -30°C (-20°F) and at least +120°C (250°F).
Grease with the correct properties is available from all major lubricant manufacturers. If the make of grease is changed and compatibility is uncertain, consult the manufacturing ABB factory, see Chapter 9.1.3 Contact information for Motors and Generators Service.
| NOTE: | Do not mix greases! There must be only one type of grease inside the bearing - not a mixture of two or more greases. |
| - | - |
| NOTE: | Grease additives are recommended. However, a written guarantee should be obtained from the lubricant manufacturer stating that the additives do not damage the bearings or the properties of the grease in the field of the operating temperature. This is especially important for EP additives. |
| NOTE: | Lubricants containing EP admixtures are not recommended. |

[2] ABB Manual for Induction Motors and Generators EN, p. 86 · Automatic re-greasing
A variety of automatic re-lubrication systems is available on the market. However, ABB recommends only the use of electromechanical re-lubrication systems. The quality of the grease entering the bearing has to be checked at least once per year: the grease has to look and feel like new grease. Any separation of the base oil from the soap is not acceptable.
NOTE:
If an automatic re-greasing system is used, double the amount of grease indicated on the bearing plate.

[3] ABB Manual for Induction Motors and Generators EN, p. 66 · Figure 32 Example of lubrication channel through bearing arrangement of horizontal machine
NOTE:
NOTE:
Start-up greasing may take several grease portions (3-10 times amount mentioned at the lubrication plate).
The re-lubrication interval will never be longer than 12 months.
The type of original grease used is found on the bearing plate on the machine. Acceptable types of grease can be found in Chapter 7.5.3 Rolling bearings.
NOTE:
Do not mix greases! There must be only one type of grease inside the bearing - not mixture of two or more greases.
The temperature of the bearings will initially increase because of the excess grease. After few hours, the excess grease will be discharged through the lubrication valve and the temperature of the bearing will return to normal running temperature.
If available, and after the machine has been running for several hours, measure the vibrations or SPM-values from the SPM-nipples, and record the values for future reference use.
Following chapter for bearing type: Sleeve bearing

[4] ABB Manual for Induction Motors and Generators EN, p. 87 · 7.5.3.6 Bearing maintenance
The lifetime of the bearings is likely to be shorter than the lifetime of the electrical machine. Therefore, the bearings will have to be changed periodically.
The maintenance of rolling bearings requires special care, tools and arrangements as to ensure a long lifetime of newly fitted bearings.
During bearing maintenance, ensure that:
- No dirt or foreign debris is allowed to enter the bearings at any time during the maintenance.
- The bearings are washed, dried and pre-greased with suitable and high quality rolling bearing grease before assembly.
- The disassembly and mounting of the bearings does not damage the bearings. The bearings must be removed by using pullers and fitted by heating, or using special tools for the purpose.
If there is a need to change bearings, please contact ABB Motors and Generators Service. See Motors and Generators contact information in Chapter 9.1.3 Contact information for Motors and Generators Service.

[5] ABB Manual for Induction Motors and Generators EN, p. 87 · Rolling bearing grease for extreme temperatures
If the bearing operating temperature is above 100°C (210°F), please consult the manufacturing ABB factory for suitable greases.

results.question: According to the Kohler KD27V12 manual's TBN chart (Fig. 27), below what TBN should the engine oil be exchanged as soon as possible?
results.rewritten_query: What is the minimum TBN value for engine oil exchange according to the TBN chart (Fig. 27) in the Kohler KD27V12 manual?
results.answer:
According to the Kohler Generator manual's TBN chart (Fig. 27), the engine oil should be exchanged as soon as possible if the TBN drops below 8 mg KOH/g.

### Likely Causes
- The combustion gases are influenced by the sulfur content in the fuel, which can lead to a decrease in TBN.
- The presence of high sulfur content in the fuel necessitates the use of high-ash engine oils.

### Procedure
1. Monitor the TBN level of the engine oil regularly.
2. If the TBN level drops below 8 mg KOH/g, plan for an immediate oil change.
3. Ensure using high-ash engine oil if the fuel has higher sulfur content.
4. Follow the specifications outlined for changing the engine oil to maintain engine performance and reduce harmful emissions.

For reference, here are the relevant values from the context:

| TBN Level (mg KOH/g) | Action                              |
|----------------------|-------------------------------------|
| < 8                  | Exchange engine oil as soon as possible |

results.question: Per NEMA MG1 as listed in the Siemens vertical motor manual, what is the unfiltered vibration limit for a resiliently mounted motor at 1800 RPM?
results.rewritten_query: What is the unfiltered vibration limit for a resiliently mounted Siemens vertical motor at 1800 RPM according to NEMA MG1 standards?
results.answer:
The unfiltered vibration limit for a resiliently mounted motor at 1800 RPM is 0.15 in/s peak (3.8 mm/s) as specified in the NEMA MG1 standards listed in the Siemens manual for vertical induction motors.

### Vibration Limit Table

| Speed, RPM | Rotational Frequency/Hz | Velocity, in/s Peak (mm/s) |
|-------------|--------------------------|-----------------------------|
| 1800       | 30                       | 0.15 (3.8)                  |

If vibration exceeds this limit, consider the following actions:

1. **Check End Play**: After tightening all flange mounting bolts, ensure that the end play is within acceptable limits.
2. **Run Unit**: Operate the motor at a minimum load.
3. **Monitor Vibration**: Measure the vibration levels.
4. **Adjust If Necessary**: If vibration is excessive:
   - Loosen the flange mounting bolts and shift the motor within the mounting flange clearance.
   - If the shifting does not resolve the issue, check the shaft alignment and the system's reed frequency.

These steps should help in identifying and mitigating excessive vibration issues. If further details are needed on shaft alignment or reed frequency checking procedures, that information is not provided in the context.

Question: Please explain the limits of bearing housing vibration.
Answer: The following limits of vibration pertain to uncoupled, resiliently mounted machines, running at no load. For machines tested with rigid mounting, the values given should be multiplied by 0.8. Vibration levels given here refer to internally excited vibration only. Motors as installed (in situ) may exhibit higher levels.
Figures 10a and 10b, taken from NEMA MG17.08, show limits for bearing housing vibration levels of machines resiliently mounted for both unfiltered and filtered measurements.

[5] Nidec Motor Manual, p. 39 · Machine Mounting
Question: Does a machine's mounting style affect its vibration?
Answer: Yes. When evaluating the vibration of electrical machines, it is important to understand the machine's mounting because mounting and vibration are closely linked. Two passive (admit insignificant external disturbances to the machine) methods of mounting a motor are resilient mounting and rigid mounting. Following is a brief description of each, and an explanation of their affect on vibration.
Resilient Mounting: Resilient mounting entails suspending the machine on a spring, or mounting it on some type of elastic support (rubber, springs, etc.). Natural oscillation frequencies of the suspension system and machine should be less than 25 percent of the frequency corresponding to the lowest speed of the machine under test. The effective mass of the elastic support should be no greater than 10 percent of that of the machine, in order to reduce the influence of the mass and the moments of inertia of these parts on the vibration level.
Rigid Mounting: Rigid mounting entails fastening the machine directly to a relatively massive foundation. According to NEMA MG17.06, a relatively massive foundation is one that has a vibration which is limited, during testing, to 0.02 in/s peak (0.5 mm/s peak) above any background vibrations. The horizontal and vertical natural frequencies of the complete test arrangement shall not coincide within +10 percent of the rotational frequency of the machine, within +5 percent of two times the rotational frequency, or within +5 percent of oneand two- times the electrical-line frequency.

results.question: For a Siemens vertical motor with a solid shaft, what total indicator readings are acceptable for parallel and angular alignment?
results.expected_answer: Parallel: total indicator reading not over 0.002 inches; angular: not over 0.002 in. per foot of radius to the dial indicator
results.rewritten_query: What are the acceptable total indicator readings for parallel and angular alignment of a Siemens vertical motor with a solid shaft?
results.answer:
For a Siemens vertical motor with a solid shaft, the acceptable total indicator readings for alignment are:

- **Parallel alignment**: Total indicator readings must not exceed **0.002 inches**.
- **Angular alignment**: Total indicator readings must not exceed **0.002 in./ft. radius to dial indicator**.

### Likely Causes for Misalignment
- Improper installation or leveling.
- Wear and tear on components.
- Thermal expansion affecting alignment.
- Foundation settling or shifting.

### Procedure for Checking Alignment
1. **Set Up**: Mount a dial indicator as shown in the provided figure.
2. **Zero the Readings**: Set the indicator dial to zero at the starting point.
3. **Rotate Couplings**: Slowly turn both coupling halves a complete turn.
4. **Measure**: Observe the dial reading at 90-degree increments from the starting point.
5. **Evaluate**: 
   - Check that total indicator readings for parallel alignment do not exceed **0.002 inches**.
   - Confirm that total indicator readings for angular alignment do not exceed **0.002 in./ft. radius to dial indicator**.

This precise alignment is crucial to prevent vibrations and potential damage to the motor and connected equipment.

results.question: After regreasing a Siemens vertical motor's bearing, how long should the motor run before the drain plug is re-installed?
results.expected_answer: At least one (1) hour, to expel excess grease from the drain opening
results.rewritten_query: After regreasing a Siemens vertical motor's bearing, how long should the motor run before reinstalling the drain plug?
results.answer:
After regreasing a Siemens vertical motor's bearing, the motor should run for at least one (1) hour before the drain plug is re-installed to allow any excess grease to be expelled from the drain opening [2]. 

### Procedure to Relubricate Bearings
1. Stop the motor and lock out the switch.
2. Thoroughly clean the grease inlet fitting or plug.
3. Remove the drain plug and clean any hardened grease from the drain.
4. Slowly pump the correct amount of grease into the grease inlet as specified on the lubrication plate.
5. Start the motor and allow it to run for at least one (1) hour to expel any excess grease.
6. Stop the motor and lock out the switch again.
7. Re-install the drain plug.
8. Put the motor back in operation.

[1] Siemens Manual Vertical Induction Motors EN, p. 5 · Temporary Storage
If the equipment is not to be installed and operated soon after arrival, store it in a clean, dry, well- ventilated place, free from vibration and rapid or wide variations in temperature. Rotate the shaft a minimum of 10 complete turns by hand each month to coat the bearings with lubricant which will retard oxidation or corrosion, and prevent possible false brinelling. If drain plugs are provided in enclosed motors, they must be removed periodically to drain any water accumulation from the motor. Consider a unit in storage when:
1. It has been delivered to the job site and is awaiting installation.
2. It has been installed but operation is delayed over 30 days pending completion of plant construction.
3. There are long (30 day) periods between operating cycles.
4. The plant (or department) is shut down for 30 days.
5. Energize space heaters, if supplied.

[2] Siemens Manual Vertical Induction Motors EN, p. 20 · Maintenance
For best results, grease should be compounded of a polyurea type and a good grade of petroleum oil and stabilized against oxidation.
The frequency of relubricating bearings and the amount added each time depends on two factors - speed and service.
All grease lube bearing motors will have affixed a plate with lubricating instructions. The instructions on this plate should be followed to achieve optimum bearing life and to avoid consequential damage to rotating parts.
Relubricate with the type of grease specified on the lubrication plate mounted on the motor, or compatible grease. Mixing of non-compatible greases can cause bearing failure.
Relubricate bearings with the proper grade of grease as follows:
1. Stop the motor and lock out the switch.
2. Thoroughly clean the grease inlet fitting or plug. If the motor has a plug, remove plug and clean the inlet.
3. Remove the drain plug (and overflow plug, if so equipped) and clean out any hardened grease.
4. Slowly pump the correct amount of grease into the grease inlet, per the lubrication plate mounted on the motor. Replace inlet plug (and overflow plug, if so equipped).
5. Start motor and allow to run at least one (1) hour to expel any excess grease from the drain opening before re-installing the drain plug.
6. Stop the motor and lock out the switch.
7. Re-install the drain plug.
8. Put the motor back in operation.

[3] Nidec Motor Manual, p. 29 · Lubrication Instructions
Question: How can motors in service be relubricated?
Answer Units are pre-lubricated at the factory and do not require initial lubrication. Relubricating interval depends upon speed, type of bearing and service. Refer to table in the Operating and Instruction Manual provided with motor for suggested re-greasing intervals and recommended greases. Operating conditions may dictate more frequent lubrication. Motor must be at rest and electrical controls should be locked open to prevent energizing while motor is being serviced (refer to section on Safety). If motor is being taken out of storage, refer to storage procedures.
To re-lubricate bearings, remove the drain plug. Inspect grease drain and remove any blockage with a mechanical probe taking care not to damage bearing. Under no circumstances should a mechanical probe be used while the motor is in operation. Add new grease at the grease inlet. New grease must be compatible with grease already in the motor (refer to Table 1 in Operating & Maintenance Manual for replenishment quantities). Run the motor for 15 to 30 minutes with the drain plug removed to allow purging of any excess grease. Shut off unit and replace the drain plug. Return motor to service.

[4] Siemens Manual Vertical Induction Motors EN, p. 20 · NOTE
If unit has been in operation for several years the old grease can harden. If this occurs remove bolts holding bottom inside end cap, raise end cap and wipe out hardened grease. Reassemble and add a small amount of fresh grease.
If machine is a totally-enclosed or weather-protected type disassembly of the lower bearing may be required to remove old grease. Also clean and refill inlet, overflow, and drain grease pipes.
Because the lower bearing is single shielded, the grease will not pass through the drain port unless the motor is run for some time.

results.rewritten_query: What grease does Siemens recommend for vertical induction motor bearings?
results.answer:
Siemens recommends using grease compounded of a polyurea type with a good grade of petroleum oil for the bearings of its vertical induction motors. The specific grease type can be confirmed by the lubrication plate mounted on the motor, which will include instructions on the proper grade of grease and its compatibility with existing lubricants [1]. 

To ensure optimal bearing life and avoid consequential damage to rotating parts, follow these guidelines:

- **Grease Composition:**
  - Polyurea type compounded with high-quality petroleum oil.
- **Compatibility:**
  - Ensure the grease is specified on the lubrication plate or is compatible with it. Mixing non-compatible greases can cause bearing failure [1].

**Procedure for Relubrication:**
1. Stop the motor and lock out the switch.
2. Thoroughly clean the grease inlet fitting or plug. If the motor has a plug, remove it and clean the inlet.
3. Remove the drain plug (and overflow plug, if equipped) and clean out any hardened grease.
4. Slowly pump the correct amount of grease into the grease inlet, as per the lubrication plate mounted on the motor. Replace the inlet plug (and overflow plug, if equipped).
5. Start the motor and allow it to run for at least one (1) hour to expel any excess grease from the drain opening before re-installing the drain plug.
6. Stop the motor and lock out the switch.
7. Re-install the drain plug.
8. Put the motor back in operation [1].

results.question: When drying a Siemens vertical motor's stator by circulating direct current, how much current and DC voltage are usually needed?
results.expected_answer: Usually 50 to 100% of full load current; the DC voltage is 0.25–5.0% of normal voltage per phase (0.50–3.25% of the rating in power)
results.rewritten_query: What are the recommended direct current and voltage levels for drying a Siemens vertical motor's stator?
results.answer:
When drying a Siemens vertical motor's stator by circulating direct current, the required current and DC voltage are as follows:

- **Current:** 50 to 100% of full load current
- **DC Voltage:** 0.25 - 5.0% of the normal voltage per phase

This allows for the necessary temperature to be achieved for effective drying of the windings without risking damage to the insulation. The corresponding power will be 0.50 - 3.25% of the rating [2]. 

### Procedure for Circulating DC during Drying
1. Remove bearing housings.
2. Center the rotor in the stator core or remove the rotor.
3. Wedge fiber strips into the lower part of the air gap to prevent rotor contact with stator core, if the rotor is left in place.
4. Attach temperature indicators to the windings, ensuring that the drying temperatures do not exceed those listed in the Insulation Drying Temperature table.
5. Connect an external current source (e.g., portable low voltage motor-generator set).
6. Monitor the conditions and adjust the setup as necessary to maintain safe temperatures.

Additionally, it is important to frequently check the temperature of connections during operation to prevent overheating and damage to insulation.

5. Attach temperature indicators to windings. Do not exceed the drying temperatures in the Insulation Drying Temperature table.
6. An external source of current can be used to circulate direct current through the winding of any type of alternating current motor. A portable low voltage motor-generator set, such as is used for welding, is usually suitable.

[2] Siemens Manual Vertical Induction Motors EN, p. 19 · High temperatures.
May cause damage to insulation.
Avoid hot spots and radiant type heat When this method is used on the stator, the stator phases may be connected in series or in parallel to suit the available power supply if both ends of all phases are accessible. If only three leads are brought out of the motor, the current may be circulated between one terminal and the other two connected together. If this is done, the temperature of the single lead connection must be checked frequently, and it is desirable to shift the leads occasionally. Usually 50 to 100% of full load current will produce the required temperature. The dc voltage required for this current will be 0.25 - 5.0% of the normal voltage per phase, and the corresponding power will be 0.50 - 3.25% of the rating.
Alternating current can be used on the stators of squirrel cage induction motors if the rotors are removed. Alternating current is usually not as easy to control as required voltage control, and a.c. requires a higher voltage source, approximately 10 to 30% of the rated winding voltage. In addition, care must be taken that miscellaneous parts adjacent to the windings, such as lead studs, core supporting member, etc., do no overheat due to induced currents and the lack of normal ventilation.
May cause damage to insulation.
Avoid hot spots and radiant type heat

[3] Siemens Manual Vertical Induction Motors EN, p. 19 · Electric Strip Heater Drying
1. Remove bearing housings.
2. Remove rotor.
3. Direct a fan on stator to carry away the moisture.
4. Attach temperature indicators to winding and apply heat as specified in the Insulation Drying Temperature table and follow procedures described for drying insulation.
5. Radiant type heaters are not recommended because some parts may become scorched before remote parts reach desired temperature.

[4] Siemens Manual Vertical Induction Motors EN, p. 10 · Dielectric (Hi-Pot) Tests
All motors receive a factory dielectric test in accordance with ANSI and IEEE Standards.
Dielectric testing may result in personal injury or death.
Operate dielectric test equipment only with qualified personnel, in accordance with manufacturer's instructions.
If a dielectric test is made on an old or repaired winding, to evaluate service reliability, the test voltage applied may vary from the rated terminal voltage to some higher value. The factory should be consulted when establishing the test voltage and procedure for testing old or repaired equipment.

[5] ABB Manual for Induction Motors and Generators EN, p. 94 · 7.6.5 Insulation resistance measurement for auxiliaries
To ensure correct operation of the machines protections and other auxiliaries, their condition can be determined by an insulation resistance test. The procedure is described in detail in Chapter 7.6 Maintenance of stator and rotor windings. The test voltage for the space heater should be 500 VDC and for other auxiliaries 100 VDC. The insulation resistance measurement for Pt-100 detectors or proximity probes is not recommended.

[1] Siemens Manual Vertical Induction Motors EN, p. 5 · Temporary Storage
If the equipment is not to be installed and operated soon after arrival, store it in a clean, dry, well- ventilated place, free from vibration and rapid or wide variations in temperature. Rotate the shaft a minimum of 10 complete turns by hand each month to coat the bearings with lubricant which will retard oxidation or corrosion, and prevent possible false brinelling. If drain plugs are provided in enclosed motors, they must be removed periodically to drain any water accumulation from the motor. Consider a unit in storage when:
1. It has been delivered to the job site and is awaiting installation.
2. It has been installed but operation is delayed over 30 days pending completion of plant construction.
3. There are long (30 day) periods between operating cycles.
4. The plant (or department) is shut down for 30 days.
5. Energize space heaters, if supplied.

[2] Nidec Motor Manual, p. 20 · Motor Inspection Procedure After Storage
Question: After storing my motor for an extended period of time, I am now ready to install it. Is there any specific inspection procedure that must be followed?
Answer: Yes. Following storage, an extensive inspection must be performed on a motor by one of our authorized service stations. This inspection must include the following elements:
- 1) Render an external inspection of the motor to assure the unit is clean, ventilation openings are free of obstructions, and no damage has occurred.
- 2) Perform a megger test of motor windings to insure satisfactory insulation resistance.
- 3) Rotate the shaft to check for roughness in bearings or interference between rotating and stationary parts.
- 4) Perform a bench test on the unit to check for excessive amp. draw, noise, or vibration.
- 5) Regrease the motor bearings (as applicable) in accordance with the unit's operating instruction folder.
- 6) The authorized service station must install a plate/tag indicating the date of inspection. Make any corrections which inspection shows to be needed.

[3] ABB Manual for Induction Motors and Generators EN, p. 49 · 3.7 Care after installation
If the machine will not be in operation for a longer period after it has been installed, the same measures as mentioned above in Chapter 2.6.1 Short term storage (less than 2 months) should be applied. Remember to rotate the shaft 10 revolutions at least every 3 months, and that self-lubricated bearings must be filled with oil. If external vibration is present, the shaft coupling should be opened and suitable rubber blocks should be placed under the feet of the machine.

[4] Siemens Manual Vertical Induction Motors EN, p. 12 · NOTE
If motor has been out of service or in storage for more than 30 days, consult Siemens Storage
Recommendations ANIM-03114, Preparation for Service

[5] Siemens Manual Vertical Induction Motors EN, p. 5 · NOTE
Storage requirements vary, depending on the length of storage and the climate. For storage periods of three months or longer or climate variations, consult Siemens Storage Recommendations ANIM-03114. Storage maintenance is to be documented for warranty information.

results.question: How should MICLAD VPI stator coils on a Siemens vertical motor be cleaned and baked?
results.expected_answer: With a quick-drying solvent and lint-free cloths, or low-pressure steam; then oven-bake the whole stator at 200°F for 12 hours and then 230°F for 12 hours
results.rewritten_query: What is the procedure for cleaning and baking MICLAD VPI stator coils in Siemens vertical motors?
results.answer:
MICLAD VPI stator coils on a Siemens vertical motor should be cleaned and baked using the following procedure:

1. Clean the coils with either:
   - A quick drying solvent and lint-free cloths, or
   - Steam clean with low-pressure steam.
2. Measure the insulation resistance of the stator windings before and after the cleaning operation.
3. Bake the entire stator as follows:
   - First, at 200°F for 12 hours.
   - Then, at 230°F for 12 hours.

For additional cleaning options, if using water and detergents, ensure they are compatible with MICLAD™ VPI insulation systems and follow the oven drying cycle as necessary [1].

MICLAD™ form wound VPI (vacuum pressure impregnated) insulated coils may be cleaned with a quick drying solvent and lint free cloths or steam cleaned with low-pressure steam, then the entire stator oven baked at 200°F for 12 hours and then 230°F for 12 hours.

1. Verify motor is clean and verify that stator and rotor ventilation passages are unobstructed.
2. Check for excessive loading or service factor.
3. Verify winding temperature rise not in excess of rated value.
4. Verify insulation resistance is above recommended minimum.
5. Verify voltage and frequency variation.
6. Check air gap.
7. Verify that bearing temperatures are within limits and that lubricant is clean and proper level maintained.
8. Verify no unusual vibration or noise exists.
9. Check alignment.
10. Check for proper lubrication.
A definite schedule of preventive maintenance inspections should be established to avoid breakdown, serious damage and extensive downtime. The schedule will depend on operating conditions and experience with similar equipment. To assure adequate maintenance, and warranty consideration, it is essential that complete records be kept for each motor including description and rating, maintenance schedule and repairs required or carried out.
This checklist does not represent an exhaustive survey of maintenance steps necessary to ensure safe operation of this equipment. Particular applications may require further procedures. Should further information be desired or should particular problems arise which are not covered sufficiently for the purchaser's purposes, the matter should be referred to the local Siemens Sales Office.
Improper maintenance can cause death, serious injury or property damage.
Use only factory authorized parts for repair of equipment. Maintenance should be performed only by qualified personnel.

Question: Is there a specific procedure which should be followed when rewinding US MOTORS® brand inverter duty motors? If so, could you please explain it.
Answer: Following are guidelines to use when rewinding US MOTORS® brand inverter duty motors:
- 1) Use inverter grade magnet wire. If not available, triple build wire may substitute.
- 2) Avoid loose windings - use slot fillers as required.
- 3) Insulate between phases, center of each coil group, both end turns and in slots.
- 4) Secure end turns - tie or band both winding ends.
- 5) Be especially careful to avoid damaging winding magnet wire.

No specific distinction or duration for long-term storage is provided in the ABB manual, which only discusses measures for when the machine is not in operation for longer periods after installation but does not clarify durations beyond short-term [2][1].

results.question: How should the re-greasing interval of an ABB machine's rolling bearings change with bearing temperature, and what is the minimum re-greasing frequency?
results.expected_answer: Intervals assume 70°C (160°F); halve them for every 15°C (30°F) increase, and they may be doubled once for a 15°C decrease; re-grease at least once per year regardless
results.rewritten_query: What is the recommended re-greasing interval for the rolling bearings of an ABB machine based on bearing temperature, and what is the minimum re-greasing frequency?
results.answer:
The re-greasing interval of an ABB machine's rolling bearings is affected by the bearing temperature as follows:

- For every 15°C (30°F) increase in bearing temperature, the re-greasing interval should be halved.
- For every 15°C (30°F) decrease in bearing temperature, the re-greasing interval may be doubled.

Regardless of the temperature, the minimum re-greasing frequency is at least once per year. This minimum frequency is stated clearly in the context. 

In summary:
- **Re-greasing Interval Adjustment**:
    - Increase in Temperature: Halve the interval.
    - Decrease in Temperature: Double the interval.
  
- **Minimum Frequency**: At least once per year [1].

contexts:
[1] ABB Manual for Induction Motors and Generators EN, p. 85 · 7.5.3.3 Re-greasing intervals
Rolling bearings of electrical machines need to be re-greased at regular intervals. The re-greasing interval is found on the bearing plate.
NOTE:
Regardless of the re-greasing interval, the bearings need to be re-greased at least once per year.
The re-greasing intervals are calculated for an operating temperature of 70°C (160°F). If the operating temperature is lower or higher than the assumed, the re-grease interval has to be altered accordingly. Higher operating temperature decreases the re-greasing interval.
NOTE:
An increase in the ambient temperature raises the temperature of the bearings correspondingly. The values for the re-greasing interval should be halved for every 15°C (30°F) increase in bearing temperature and may be once doubled for a 15°C (30°F) decrease in bearing temperature.

[2] ABB Manual for Induction Motors and Generators EN, p. 86 · Automatic re-greasing
A variety of automatic re-lubrication systems is available on the market. However, ABB recommends only the use of electromechanical re-lubrication systems. The quality of the grease entering the bearing has to be checked at least once per year: the grease has to look and feel like new grease. Any separation of the base oil from the soap is not acceptable.
NOTE:
If an automatic re-greasing system is used, double the amount of grease indicated on the bearing plate.

[3] ABB Manual for Induction Motors and Generators EN, p. 86 · 7.5.3.5 Bearing grease (table)
It is essential to use grease of good quality and with the correct base soap. This will ensure a long and trouble free lifetime of the bearings.
Grease used for re-greasing should have the following properties:
- Be special rolling bearing grease.
- Be of good quality with a lithium complex soap, and with mineral-, or PAO-oil.
- Have a base oil viscosity of 100 to 160 cSt at 40°C (105°F).
- Have a consistency NLGI grade between 1.5 and 3. For vertically or in hot conditions mounted machines, NLGI grade 2 or 3 is recommended.
- Have a continuous temperature range between -30°C (-20°F) and at least +120°C (250°F).
Grease with the correct properties is available from all major lubricant manufacturers. If the make of grease is changed and compatibility is uncertain, consult the manufacturing ABB factory, see Chapter 9.1.3 Contact information for Motors and Generators Service.
| NOTE: | Do not mix greases! There must be only one type of grease inside the bearing - not a mixture of two or more greases. |
| - | - |
| NOTE: | Grease additives are recommended. However, a written guarantee should be obtained from the lubricant manufacturer stating that the additives do not damage the bearings or the properties of the grease in the field of the operating temperature. This is especially important for EP additives. |
| NOTE: | Lubricants containing EP admixtures are not recommended. |

[4] ABB Manual for Induction Motors and Generators EN, p. 66 · Figure 32 Example of lubrication channel through bearing arrangement of horizontal machine
NOTE:
NOTE:
Start-up greasing may take several grease portions (3-10 times amount mentioned at the lubrication plate).
The re-lubrication interval will never be longer than 12 months.
The type of original grease used is found on the bearing plate on the machine. Acceptable types of grease can be found in Chapter 7.5.3 Rolling bearings.
NOTE:
Do not mix greases! There must be only one type of grease inside the bearing - not mixture of two or more greases.
The temperature of the bearings will initially increase because of the excess grease. After few hours, the excess grease will be discharged through the lubrication valve and the temperature of the bearing will return to normal running temperature.
If available, and after the machine has been running for several hours, measure the vibrations or SPM-values from the SPM-nipples, and record the values for future reference use.
Following chapter for bearing type: Sleeve bearing

[5] ABB Manual for Induction Motors and Generators EN, p. 85 · 7.5.3.4 Re-greasing
All rolling bearings of rotating electrical machines need to be re-greased, see Chapter 7.5.3.3 Re-greasing intervals. The re-greasing can be performed either manually or by means of an automatic system. In either case, it has to be verified that a suitable amount of the correct grease is entering the bearing at suitable intervals.
NOTE:
Grease can cause skin irritation and eye inflammation. Follow all safety precautions specified by the grease manufacturer.

[1] ABB Manual for Induction Motors and Generators EN, p. 85 · Manual re-greasing while the machine is running
Re-greasing while the machine is running:
- Verify that the grease to be used is suitable.
- Clean the grease nipples and the area around them.
- Verify that the lubrication channel is open, if equipped with a handle, open it.
- Press the specified amount and type of grease into the bearing.
- Let the machine run 1-2 hours in order to ensure that all excess grease is forced out of the bearing. The bearing temperature may temporarily increase during this time.
- If equipped with a handle, close it.
NOTE:
Beware of all rotating parts during the re-greasing.

[2] ABB Manual for Induction Motors and Generators EN, p. 86 · Manual re-greasing while the machine is at a standstill
Preferably, re-grease the machine while it is running. If this is not possible, or considered dangerous, the re-greasing has to be carried out while the machine is at a standstill. In this case:
- Verify that the grease to be used is suitable.
- Stop the machine.
- Clean the grease nipples and the area around them.
- Verify that the lubrication channel is open, if equipped with a handle, open it.
- Press only half the amount of the specified type of grease into the bearing.
- Run the machine for a few minutes at full speed.
- Stop the machine.
- After the machine has stopped, press the specified amount of the correct grease into the bearing.
- Let the machine run 1-2 hours in order to ensure that all excess grease is forced out of the bearing. The bearing temperature may temporarily increase during this time.
- If equipped with a handle, close it.

[3] ABB Manual for Induction Motors and Generators EN, p. 85 · 7.5.3.4 Re-greasing
All rolling bearings of rotating electrical machines need to be re-greased, see Chapter 7.5.3.3 Re-greasing intervals. The re-greasing can be performed either manually or by means of an automatic system. In either case, it has to be verified that a suitable amount of the correct grease is entering the bearing at suitable intervals.
NOTE:
Grease can cause skin irritation and eye inflammation. Follow all safety precautions specified by the grease manufacturer.

[4] ABB Manual for Induction Motors and Generators EN, p. 86 · Automatic re-greasing
A variety of automatic re-lubrication systems is available on the market. However, ABB recommends only the use of electromechanical re-lubrication systems. The quality of the grease entering the bearing has to be checked at least once per year: the grease has to look and feel like new grease. Any separation of the base oil from the soap is not acceptable.
NOTE:
If an automatic re-greasing system is used, double the amount of grease indicated on the bearing plate.

[5] ABB Manual for Induction Motors and Generators EN, p. 118 · 9.2.1 General spare part considerations
The machines manufactured by ABB are designed and manufactured to provide reliable and trouble-free operation for decades. This requires, however, that the machines are properly maintained and operated. This maintenance includes changing of parts subjected to normal wear.
There is always an inevitable amount of uncertainty related to wearing. The wear rates of these parts vary greatly according to application, environment and particular conditions. Therefore, the condition of these parts should be inspected regularly and a sufficient amount of spare parts should be kept in stock. These spares help to minimize down time if the need appears. The extent of the stock should be decided based upon the criticality of the application, the availability of the particular spare part and the recommendation of the manufacturer.

results.answer:
The resistance value for a Pt-100 detector at 100°C is 164.76 Ω according to the temperature values provided in Table 11 from the context.

| PT100 RES Ω | TEMP °C |
|-------------|---------|
| 164.76 Ω    | 100     | 
[1][3]

If you suspect a problem with the Pt-100 detector at this temperature, consider the following possible symptoms:

- Infinite or zero resistance over the detector
- Disappearance of measurement signal during or after startup
- A significantly different resistance value in a single detector

To confirm a suspected failure, follow this procedure:

1. Disconnect the cables from the detector.
2. Measure the resistance at the detector using a multimeter.
3. Record the findings.
4. Compare the measured resistance to the expected value (164.76 Ω at 100°C). 

This will help determine if the Pt-100 detector is functioning properly.

[2] ABB Manual for Induction Motors and Generators EN, p. 114 · 8.3.2 Pt-100 resistance temperature detectors
Pt-100 resistance temperature detectors are an essential part in the machine's condition monitoring and protection system. They are used to measure temperatures in the windings, bearings and in the cooling air. The Pt-100 detector uses a fine platinum filament for the temperature measurement, which can be damaged e.g. by incorrect handling or excessive vibration.
The following symptoms might suggest a problem in a Pt-100 detector:
- Infinite or zero resistance over the detector
- Disappearance of measurement signal during, or after start up
- A significantly different resistance value in a single detector.
If a Pt-100 failure is suspected the findings should always be confirmed from the connection box, by measuring the resistance at the detector with its cables disconnected. The findings should by registered. For the correct measuring current see the appropriate Pt-100 detector. For resistance values at different temperatures, see Table 11 Temperature values for Pt-100 elements.

results.rewritten_query: What is the recommended torque in newton-metres for an oiled M20 grade 8.8 bolt on an ABB machine?
results.answer:
An oiled M20 grade 8.8 bolt should be torqued to **360 Nm** on an ABB machine according to the general tightening torques provided. 

| Size | Tightening torque in Nm (oiled) | 
| - | - | 
| M20 | 360 | 

### Likely Causes for Proper Tightening
- Ensures the integrity and reliability of the machine.
- Prevents loosening over time, which can lead to severe damage.

### Procedure for Tightening
1. Ensure the bolt and threading are clean and free of debris.
2. Apply an appropriate lubricant (in this case, oil) to the threads of the bolt.
3. Tighten the M20 bolt to the specified torque value of 360 Nm.
4. Regularly check to ensure that the bolt remains tight over time to avoid loosening.

This guidance is based on the provided ABB manual for induction motors and generators, focusing on maintaining the correct torque specifications to support operational integrity [1].

results.question: On a rigidly mounted ABB machine, which RMS vibration velocity separates zone B from zone C?
results.rewritten_query: What is the RMS vibration velocity threshold that separates zone B from zone C on a rigidly mounted ABB machine?
results.answer:
The RMS vibration velocity that separates zone B from zone C for a rigidly mounted ABB machine is 4.5 mm/s, as indicated in the following table:

| Support class | Zone boundary | R.m.s. velocity [mm/s] |
| - | - | - |
| Rigid | B/C | 4.5 |

This means that when the vibration exceeds 4.5 mm/s, the machine is considered to be in an unsatisfactory condition for long-term continuous operation, classified under zone C. It is advisable to address the vibration issue before reaching more severe conditions that may lead to damage (zone D) or before the machine is operated for an extended period under these conditions, which may necessitate timely remedial actions. 

Reference for these values and their implications can be found in sources [1].

results.question: whats the lowest insulation resistance thats ok for a used stator winding on an ABB motor
results.rewritten_query: What is the minimum acceptable insulation resistance for a used stator winding in an ABB motor?
results.answer:
The lowest acceptable insulation resistance for a used stator winding on an ABB motor is greater than 100 MΩ under the test conditions specified. This value applies when the insulation resistance is measured at 40 °C with the test voltage applied for 1 minute or longer [1].

### Likely Causes of Low Insulation Resistance
- Excess humidity
- Presence of dirt
- Incorrect storage or transportation conditions
- Inadequate operation practices

### Procedure for Measuring Insulation Resistance
1. Ensure the motor is disconnected from the power supply.
2. Use a hand cranked or solid state insulation resistance tester.
3. Apply a test voltage of at least 500 VDC.
4. Measure the insulation resistance for a duration of at least 1 minute.
5. Compare the measured value against the minimum value of 100 MΩ.
6. If the value is below 100 MΩ, investigate potential causes such as moisture or dirt affecting the insulation.

If further information on the measurement conditions or testing procedures is necessary, it is not provided in the context.

[1] ABB Manual for Induction Motors and Generators EN, p. 92 · 7.6.4.3 Minimum values for insulation resistance
Criteria for windings in a normal condition:
Generally, the insulation resistance values for dry windings should exceed the minimum values significantly. Definite values are impossible to give, because resistance varies depending on the machine type and local conditions. In addition, the insulation resistance is affected by the age and usage of the machine. Therefore, the following values can only be considered as guidelines.
The insulation resistance limits, which are given below, are valid at 40 °C, and when the test voltage has been applied for 1 minute or longer.
- Rotor.
For induction machines with wound rotors: R(1-10 min at 40 °C) > 5 MΩ.
NOTE:
- Stator.
For new stators: R(1-10 min at 40 °C) > 1000 MΩ. If the measuring conditions are extremely warm and humid, R(1-10 min at 40 °C) values above 100 MΩ can be accepted.
For used stators: R(1-10 min at 40 °C) > 100 MΩ.
NOTE:
If the values given here are not reached, the reason for the low insulation resistance should be determined. A low insulation resistance value is often caused by excess humidity or dirt, although the actual insulation is intact.

[2] Siemens Manual Vertical Induction Motors EN, p. 18 · Insulation Resistance
Check insulation resistance periodically. Use a hand cranked or solid state insulation resistance tester and test with at least 500 volts, but not greater than motor rated voltage.
For motors with newer insulation systems such as MICLAD™ VPI, the insulation resistance after one minute should be greater than 1000 megohms. (Values in excess of 5000 megohms are common.) For older motors, the minimum value recommended in IEEE Standard 43 can be used. The value in megohms, when corrected to 40°C, is equal to the motor rated voltage in kilovolts plus 1. For example, for a motor with a rated voltage of 2300 volts, the limit value would be:
2.3 + 1 = 3.3 (megohms).

[3] Siemens Manual Vertical Induction Motors EN, p. 10 · Insulation Resistance
Check insulation resistance prior to connecting motor to power supply. A hand cranked or solid state electronic insulation resistance tester, at least 500 volts d.c., but not over rated voltage, is usually used (see Maintenance).
See IEEE Recommended Practice for Testing Insulation Resistance Rotating Machinery IEEE Std 43.

[4] ABB Manual for Induction Motors and Generators EN, p. 90 · 7.6.4 Insulation resistance test
During general maintenance work and before the machine is started up for the first time or after a long period of standstill, the insulation resistance of stator and rotor windings must be measured.
The insulation resistance measurement provides information about the humidity and dirtiness of the insulation. Based upon this information, correct cleaning and drying actions can be determined.
For new machines with dry windings, the insulation resistance is very high. The resistance can, however, be extremely low if the machine has been subjected to incorrect transportation and storage conditions and humidity, or if the machine is operated incorrectly.
NOTE:
Windings should be earthed briefly immediately after measurement in order to avoid risk of electric shock.

[5] ABB Manual for Induction Motors and Generators EN, p. 94 · 7.6.5 Insulation resistance measurement for auxiliaries
To ensure correct operation of the machines protections and other auxiliaries, their condition can be determined by an insulation resistance test. The procedure is described in detail in Chapter 7.6 Maintenance of stator and rotor windings. The test voltage for the space heater should be 500 VDC and for other auxiliaries 100 VDC. The insulation resistance measurement for Pt-100 detectors or proximity probes is not recommended.

results.question: Roughly how many direct-on-line starts per year is an ABB induction machine designed for?
results.rewritten_query: What is the recommended limit for direct-on-line starts per year for an ABB induction machine?
results.answer:
Roughly, an ABB induction machine is designed for a maximum of **1000 direct-on-line starts per year** in typical applications. This value is contingent on the load characteristics, including the torque curve versus rotational speed and inertia, as well as the machine type and design. Excessive starts can lead to increased temperatures and stress on the machine, potentially resulting in shorter lifespan and failures. 

To determine the exact number of allowable consecutive or annual starts for a specific machine, refer to the performance data sheet or consult the manufacturer for detailed information about the machine's starting frequency based on its load characteristics [1].

results.question: For ABB flood-lubricated sleeve bearings, what oil feed pressure is considered normal?
results.rewritten_query: What is the normal oil feed pressure for ABB flood-lubricated sleeve bearings?
results.answer:
The normal supply pressure for ABB flood-lubricated sleeve bearings is 125 kPa ± 25 kPa (18 psi ± 4 psi) to ensure the appropriate flow of oil to the bearing. It is important to maintain this pressure as higher supply pressure does not provide additional benefits and may cause oil leakages from the bearing [4]. 

**Procedure for Checking Oil Supply Pressure:**
1. Verify the oil supply pressure using the pressure valve and orifice.
2. Ensure the pressure is set to 125 kPa ± 25 kPa (18 psi ± 4 psi).
3. Monitor the oil flow rate, which should be specified in the dimensional drawing.
4. Adjust the pressure as necessary to maintain the correct flow to the bearings.

**Key Considerations:**
- High supply pressure does not provide benefits but increases the risk of oil leakages.
- Continuous monitoring of oil levels and conditions is critical for the reliable operation of the bearing [5].

Verify that no rotating parts rub against any stationary parts. Verify through the oil sight glass that the oil level inside bearing is correct. The correct oil level is in the middle of the oil sight glass, but as long as the oil level is within the oil sight glass, the level is acceptable.
Check the temperature and the oil level of the bearings continuously in the beginning. This is particularly important for self-lubricating bearings. If the machine is under warranty, the manufacturing factory must always be contacted before any action is taken.
For self-lubricating bearings, the rotation of the oil ring is verified through the inspection window on top of the bearing. If the oil ring is not rotating, the machine must be stopped immediately, as a stopped oil ring will result in bearing failure.
For flood-lubricated machines, the oil supply pressure is adjusted with the pressure valve and orifice. The normal supply pressure is 125 kPa ± 25 kPa (18 psi ± 4 psi). This gives the right flow of oil to the bearing. Using higher supply pressure gives no additional benefit, but can cause bearing oil leakages. The rate of oil flow is also specified on the dimensional drawing.
NOTE:

[5] ABB Manual for Induction Motors and Generators EN, p. 82 · 7.5.1 Sleeve bearings
In normal operating conditions, sleeve bearings require little maintenance. To ensure reliable operation, the oil level and the amount of oil leakage should be regularly checked.

results.question: ABB class F stator - minimum PI?
results.rewritten_query: What is the minimum insulation resistance value for an ABB Class F stator?
results.answer:
The minimum polarization index (PI) value for ABB class F stator windings is more than 2 [5]. 

### Likely Causes or Reasoning
- A PI value close to 1 indicates that the windings are humid and dirty, which can impair insulation performance.

### Procedure
1. Measure the insulation resistance after applying the voltage for:
   - 15 seconds
   - 1 minute
2. Calculate the PI by dividing the insulation resistance measured at 1 minute by that at 15 seconds.
3. Ensure the winding temperature is below 50ºC (122ºF) to avoid unreliable readings.

No further details or numerical calculations were provided in the context regarding the measurement procedure or thresholds.
